title: The framework claims boundary: the checker's own rules
note: tools/claims_enforcement.py holds each boundary of CLAIMS_BOUNDARY.md to code that defines it and tests that exist (directive 14); each rule it applies is removed here and tests/test_claims_boundary.py must notice.

for is_, is_not in REQUIRED:
        if not any(
mutations.replace:

mutations.rationale: a required boundary can be dropped and the registry still passes

mutations.name: CB2_a_required_boundary_forgotten
mutations.rationale: the checker's own list loses a boundary behind a repeat of another, the count unchanged; the registry may then lose it too

mutations.name: CB3_naming_both_terms_is_enough
mutations.find: return bool(sep) and is_ in head and is_not in tail
mutations.replace:
s = statement.lower()
    return is_ in s and is_not in s
mutations.rationale: an inverted or reversed statement registers the boundary it denies

mutations.name: CB4_the_negated_term_is_not_read
mutations.find: return bool(sep) and is_ in head and is_not in tail
mutations.replace: return bool(sep) and is_ in head
mutations.rationale: a simulation result is not a surrogate registers 'not a measurement'

mutations.name: CB5_every_symbol_is_defined
mutations.replace:
def _defined(module: Path, symbol: str) -> bool:
    return True
mutations.rationale: a registry naming code that does not exist passes

mutations.name: CB9_a_missing_module_is_silent
mutations.rationale: a registry naming a module that does not exist passes

mutations.name: CB10_any_test_in_the_file_will_do

mutations.name: CB11_no_test_is_fine
mutations.rationale: a boundary no test holds passes

mutations.name: CB12_no_code_is_fine
mutations.rationale: a boundary no code enforces passes

mutations.name: CB15_a_duplicate_is_not_noticed
mutations.rationale: one boundary registered twice passes as two
